$comment: Phase 32A. Quotes for every withdrawal value on plugins/animal-health/*.json, keyed pluginId → withdrawal.<speciesId>.<class>.<meatDays|milkHours|eggsDays|doNotUseFor>. Each entry is { url, publisher, date, quote, note? } read from the product label (FDA Animal Drugs @ FDA, DailyMed or the manufacturer label). A product ships only once every food species on its label has a sourced withdrawal. See docs/research/label-research-prompt.md Task 9.

prohibitedExtraLabel.publisher: eCFR, 21 CFR 530.41 Drugs prohibited for extralabel use in animals
prohibitedExtraLabel.quote: (a) The following drugs, families of drugs, and substances are prohibited for extralabel animal and human drug uses in food-producing animals. (1) Chloramphenicol; (2) Clenbuterol; (3) Diethylstilbestrol (DES); (4) Dimetridazole; (5) Ipronidazole; (6) Other nitroimidazoles; (7) Furazolidone. (8) Nitrofurazone. (9) Sulfonamide drugs in lactating dairy cattle (except approved use of sulfadimethoxine, sulfabromomethazine, and sulfaethoxypyridazine); (10) Fluoroquinolones; and (11) Glycopeptides. (12) Phenylbutazone in female dairy cattle 20 months of age or older. (13) Cephalosporins (not including cephapirin) in cattle, swine, chickens, or turkeys: (i) For disease prevention purposes; (ii) At unapproved doses, frequencies, durations, or routes of administration; or (iii) If the drug is not approved for that species and production class. (b) ... [Reserved] (c) [Reserved] (d) The following drugs, or classes of drugs, that are approved for treating or preventing influenza A, are prohibited from extralabel use in chickens, turkeys, and ducks: (1) Adamantanes. (2) Neuraminidase inhibitors.
prohibitedExtraLabel.note: Text fetched from the eCFR versioner API (title 21, part 530, section 530.41), current through 2026-09-28; last substantive amendment 2016-12-31 (77 FR 745, Jan. 6, 2012 is the last cited rulemaking). Paragraph (b) is [Reserved] (nonfood animals); the influenza A drugs are paragraph (d), not (b).

withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.publisher: Merck Animal Health, Safe-Guard (fenbendazole) Suspension 10% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.quote: Cattle must not be slaughtered for human consumption within 8 days following last treatment with this drug product.

withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.milkHo.publisher: Merck Animal Health, Safe-Guard (fenbendazole) Suspension 10% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.milkHo.quote: Milk taken from cows during treatment and for 48 hours after the last treatment must not be used for human consumption.

withdrawal.goat.all.meatDays.publisher: Merck Animal Health, Safe-Guard (fenbendazole) Suspension 10% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.goat.all.meatDays.quote: Goats must not be slaughtered for human consumption within 6 days following last treatment with this drug product.

withdrawal.goat.lactating-dairy.doNotUse.publisher: Merck Animal Health, Safe-Guard (fenbendazole) Suspension 10% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.goat.lactating-dairy.doNotUse.quote: Because a milk discard time has not been established, do not use in lactating goats.

withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec (ivermectin) Injection label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.quote: Do not treat cattle within 35 days of slaughter.

withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec (ivermectin) Injection label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.quote: Because a withdrawal time in milk has not been established, do not use in female dairy cattle of breeding age.
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.note: The label says female dairy cattle of breeding age; read here as lactating dairy, the stricter of the two.

withdrawal.pig.all.meatDays.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec (ivermectin) Injection label, DailyMed
withdrawal.pig.all.meatDays.quote: Do not treat swine within 18 days of slaughter.

withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec Pour-On (ivermectin topical solution) label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.quote: Cattle must not be treated within 48 days of slaughter for human consumption.

withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec Pour-On (ivermectin topical solution) label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.quote: Because a withdrawal time in milk has not been established, do not use in female dairy cattle of breeding age.
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.note: The label says female dairy cattle of breeding age; read here as lactating dairy, the stricter of the two.

withdrawal.sheep.all.meatDays.publisher: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, Ivomec (ivermectin) Drench label, DailyMed
withdrawal.sheep.all.meatDays.quote: Do not treat sheep within 11 days of slaughter.

withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.publisher: Huvepharma, Prohibit (levamisole hydrochloride) Soluble Drench Powder label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.quote: Do not administer to cattle within 48 hours of slaughter for food.

withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.publisher: Huvepharma, Prohibit (levamisole hydrochloride) Soluble Drench Powder label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.quote: To prevent residues in milk, do not administer to dairy animals of breeding age.
withdrawal.cattle.lactating-dairy.doNotU.note: The label says dairy animals of breeding age; read here as lactating dairy, the stricter of the two.

withdrawal.sheep.all.meatDays.publisher: Huvepharma, Prohibit (levamisole hydrochloride) Soluble Drench Powder label, DailyMed
withdrawal.sheep.all.meatDays.quote: Do not administer to sheep within 72 hours of slaughter for food.

withdrawal.sheep.lactating-dairy.doNotUs.publisher: Huvepharma, Prohibit (levamisole hydrochloride) Soluble Drench Powder label, DailyMed
withdrawal.sheep.lactating-dairy.doNotUs.quote: To prevent residues in milk, do not administer to dairy animals of breeding age.
withdrawal.sheep.lactating-dairy.doNotUs.note: The label says dairy animals of breeding age without naming a species; applied to sheep as the stricter reading.

withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.publisher: Huvepharma, Corid (amprolium oral solution) 9.6% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.quote: No withdrawal period is required when used according to labeling.
withdrawal.cattle.all.meatDays.note: The label states no withdrawal period at all; only meat is recorded because the label's uses are calves, growing beef cattle and replacement heifers under one year, and it names no milk time.

withdrawal.chicken.all.meatDays.publisher: Huvepharma, Amprol (amprolium oral solution) 9.6% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.chicken.all.meatDays.quote: No withdrawal period is required when used according to labeling.
withdrawal.chicken.all.meatDays.note: The label names growing chickens, turkeys and laying hens.

withdrawal.chicken.all.eggsDays.publisher: Huvepharma, Amprol (amprolium oral solution) 9.6% label, DailyMed
withdrawal.chicken.all.eggsDays.quote: No withdrawal period is required when used according to labeling.
withdrawal.chicken.all.eggsDays.note: The label names laying hens among the animals it is for.
